title: Dynamic Programming
description: Learn to recognize, derive, implement, and analyze dynamic programming patterns.
learning_objectives: Derive an optimized solution from a naive baseline

sections.title: Recognition and core idea
sections.markdown:
## When to recognize this pattern
Look for problems with overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure, repeated work, or a prompt whose constraints rule out a quadratic scan.

## Core idea
Dynamic programming applies when subproblems overlap and the solution has optimal substructure. Define the state, base case, and transition before coding. Top-down memoization caches recursive states; bottom-up tabulation fills a DP table in dependency order.
key_points: Recognition: problems with overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure.
State the invariant before choosing code.

sections.title: From naive to better
sections.learning_objective: Derive the optimized approach from a baseline.
sections.markdown:
## Naive approach
Start with exponential repeated recursion. It may be easy to verify, but it repeats work and becomes too slow as input grows. State its cost before optimizing.

## Better approach
Use top-down memoization or bottom-up tabulation. The optimization is valid only if the invariant proves discarded work cannot affect the answer. Never quote a complexity without identifying the operation that dominates it.

sections.title: Complexity and common mistakes
sections.markdown:
## Time complexity
O(n) time. Explain whether sorting or preprocessing is included.

## Space complexity
O(n) DP table space, reducible to O(1). Input storage does not count as auxiliary space unless copied.

## Common mistakes
Using the pattern without its precondition, moving state in the wrong order, missing empty input, mishandling duplicates, and reporting average-case cost as a guarantee. For recursion, include call-stack space; for a DP table or hash map, count stored states.
key_points: Space: O(n) DP table space, reducible to O(1).

sections.title: Arena transfer practice
sections.learning_objective: Transfer the pattern without copying a solution.
sections.markdown:
## Arena reference
Practice with `dsa-min-cost-climbing-stairs` in Forge Arena. First restate the invariant and complexity target, then implement from a blank editor. If stuck, use progressive hints only after writing the naive approach. After submission, test one normal case, one boundary case, and one adversarial case. Arena correctness is deterministic; an explanation is useful only when it matches the code's behavior.
key_points: Independent recall is stronger evidence than assisted completion.
